title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 7th District
area: Western and northwestern Minnesota, including Moorhead, Willmar, Alexandria and the Red River Valley farm country.

context.text: Incumbent Michelle Fischbach (R) advanced from the August 11, 2026 Republican primary. Erik Osberg won the Democratic primary over Steve Carlson.

candidates.name: Michelle Fischbach
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the August 11, 2026 Republican primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2021); Chair, Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee

summary.text: Fischbach is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 7th District, first elected in 2020. A longtime Minnesota state senator, she became the first woman to serve as president of the Minnesota Senate and served as Minnesota's lieutenant governor in 2018-2019. In the House she serves on the Ways and Means and Rules committees and chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee.

background.text: Grew up in Woodbury, Minnesota, and graduated from Woodbury High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and economics from St. Cloud State University and a law degree from William Mitchell College of Law.
Was elected in 1994 as the first woman on the Paynesville city council, according to Wikipedia; she and her husband, Scott, have lived in the Paynesville area.
Was elected to the Minnesota Senate in a 1996 special election and served until 2018, including as chair of the Senate Higher Education Committee.
In 2011 became the first woman in Minnesota history to serve as President of the Minnesota Senate, a post she held until 2013 and again from 2017.

Became the 49th Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota in 2018 after Lt. Gov. Tina Smith was appointed to the U.S. Senate, since the Senate president is next in the line of succession; she served until January 2019.
Won the 2020 election for Minnesota's 7th District, defeating Democratic incumbent Collin Peterson, and took office in January 2021.
Currently serves on the Committee on Rules, where she chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee, and on the Committee on Ways and Means.

Her official biography lists agriculture, 2nd Amendment rights, respect for law and order, and defending the unborn as issues that matter most to her district; she and her husband, Scott, have two children and seven grandchildren and live on a hobby farm in the Paynesville area.

priorities.text: Chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee and serves on the Committee on Ways and Means (Oversight and Trade subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Previously served on the Committee on Agriculture, including as ranking member of the Subcommittee on Commodity Exchanges, Energy, and Credit.

positions.summary: Opposed 2021 bills expanding background checks on firearm transfers, saying they would restrict the rights of law-abiding gun owners.
positions.quote: I oppose any attempt to restrict the constitutional rights of law-abiding Americans, and that’s exactly what these bills do.

positions.summary: Supported the Secure the Border Act, which would restart border wall construction, deploy more Border Patrol agents, and end catch-and-release.
positions.quote: Republicans are listening to the people of this country and are committed to securing our border and putting a stop to this immigration crisis.

positions.summary: Supported an Israel security supplemental appropriations package to fund Iron Dome defenses and replenish Israeli military stockpiles.
positions.quote: This emergency supplemental package is critical to supporting Israel as they defend themselves against terrorism. It would reinforce the Iron Dome defense systems, replenish Israel's domestic defense stockpiles, and protect U.S. citizens.

positions.summary: Introduced legislation creating federal education grants to recruit and retain law enforcement officers.
positions.quote: I am proud to introduce the Law Enforcement Education Grant Program Act to inspire the next generation and establish a targeted approach to specifically invest in well-trained and highly educated police officers.

record.text: Chairs the Rules and Organization of the House Subcommittee, Committee on Rules, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026); also serves on the Committee on Ways and Means (Oversight and Trade subcommittees).
Served on the House Committee on Budget and the Committee on Ethics during the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Served as ranking member of the Agriculture Subcommittee on Commodity Exchanges, Energy, and Credit during the 117th Congress (2021-2022).
Introduced the Law Enforcement Education Grant Program Act, providing federal grants to students pursuing a first degree in law enforcement or criminal justice in exchange for a service commitment.

candidates.name: Erik Osberg
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary over Steve Carlson.

summary.text: Osberg is a Wadena resident and Otter Tail County economic development employee running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Michelle Fischbach in his first run for public office. According to his campaign, he has worked in the financial sector, public sector, media, trades and as a small business owner. He is campaigning on rural healthcare, agriculture, public education and reducing corporate influence in politics.

background.text: Graduated from Upsala Area Schools in central Minnesota and earned a college degree from Hamline University.

According to his campaign website, he has worked in the financial sector, public sector, media and the trades and was a small business owner; he describes himself as a husband, father and working-class Minnesotan.

Has lived in Wadena for about two decades and, as of March 2025, worked as the Rural Rebound Initiative coordinator for Otter Tail County; KAXE describes him as leading Otter Tail County's economic development program.
Announced his campaign for Minnesota's 7th District on March 11, 2025, at the Wadena Depot, in his first run for public office.
Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with about two-thirds of the vote against Steve Carlson.
Describes himself as 'a rural candidate for a rural district,' running to represent western Minnesota.
background.quote: He is a rural candidate for a rural district.

priorities.text: Defend constitutional rights and protect fair elections.
priorities.quote: Defend our constitutional rights, protect fair elections, and stand up for the institutions that keep power in the hands of the people.

priorities.text: Get corporate money out of politics, including a constitutional amendment ending Citizens United and a ban on individual stock trading by members of Congress.
priorities.quote: We believe in a constitutional amendment ending Citizens United. We believe in banning individual stock trading for congress.

priorities.text: Make healthcare more affordable and accessible for rural families, seniors, and communities that rely on local clinics and hospitals.
priorities.quote: Make healthcare more affordable and accessible, especially for rural families, seniors, and communities that rely on local clinics and hospitals.

priorities.text: Protect and expand federal support for public schools, students, and teachers.
priorities.quote: Protect & expand strong federal support for public schools, students, teachers, and the future of our communities.

priorities.text: Support farms, small businesses, and rural economies with federal backing for local solutions on housing, childcare, and public safety.
priorities.quote: Support farms, small businesses, local innovation, and rural economies.

positions.summary: Campaigns on making healthcare more affordable and accessible, particularly for rural communities.
positions.quote: Make healthcare more affordable and accessible, especially for rural families, seniors, and communities that rely on local clinics and hospitals.

candidates.researchNotes: Osberg has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; positions are drawn from his campaign website's priorities pages.
